column1: # These non-base SONAME declarations seed feed-provider ownership. Eligible
# source recipes must keep these versions aligned with package.env. Actual
# target ownership is verified separately against the locked image inventory.
# Audacious 4.6.1 is built once by the audited core recipe. Its three public
# libraries have one reusable runtime owner; the player and every loadable
# Audacious plugin acquire that owner through exact dependencies instead of
# copying any of these SONAMEs into their payload.
# Archive utilities add three public compression-library SONAMEs that do not
# exist in the immutable r9 firmware target. Each SONAME has one independently
# installable IPK owner; archive applications depend on them instead of copying
# a private library into a command package.
# Python's libpython is public ABI for native extension modules and therefore
# is split from the standard library data and the interpreter executable.
# jq's public library is split from the command package. This lets command
# packages declare one exact provider instead of embedding libjq privately.
# The K230 baseline enables PCRE2. Keep its public 8-bit regular-expression
# ABI in a dedicated provider; GNU grep declares the exact package dependency.
# Git's XML parsing support consumes the public Expat ABI. Keep it independently
# installable so Git never borrows a firmware or historical-release library.
# CPython _ctypes and future FFI consumers use the public libffi ABI. It is a
# dedicated source-built provider rather than a private interpreter payload.
# CPython _sqlite3 and future database clients use SQLite's public ABI. Keep
# the source-built SONAME independent of every language-runtime payload.
# CPython _decimal is configured to use the public mpdecimal ABI. It remains
# a dedicated source-built provider instead of a private interpreter payload.
# Split OpenSSL's two public SONAMEs into explicit providers before Git, curl,
# Python, or Node may depend on TLS. They are built from one locked source tree.
# Rsync consumes popt's public command-line parsing ABI. Keep it independently
# installable so rsync and future CLI parsers never carry a private copy.
# libatomic is not an ABI-seed library. Its feed provider transfers the exact
# GCC 14.1.1 object from the matching target, rather than borrowing it at run time.
# The reviewed minimal Buildroot libcurl configuration is the HTTPS transport
# provider for Git. Optional HTTP/2, libssh2, IDN, and c-ares features stay off.
# gawk has line editing enabled by the reviewed baseline. Its readable
# command-line ABI is provided in layers so the interpreter never embeds
# tmux shares libevent's four public event-loop SONAMEs with future consumers.
# The provider has OpenSSL support disabled; no TLS ABI is carried privately.
# file-type inspection has one reusable compression/runtime layer. libmagic
# is built from the file source package; its libz dependency is owned by the
# reviewed libzlib provider rather than copied from the firmware image.
# Public AI and common-library providers: SONAMEs verified from their
# independently built RISC-V ELF objects. Consumers resolve these providers
# through the normal recursive runtime dependency calculation.
